question: Urine osmolality in Diabetes insipidus is
analysis: In Diabetes insipidus, the kidneys are unable to concentrate urine due to a deficiency of antidiuretic hormone (ADH) or a lack of response to it. As a result, urine osmolality is typically low. Normal urine osmolality ranges from 500 to 800 mmol/L, so in Diabetes insipidus, it is usually less than 300 mmol/L.
